To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the P-type Ca(2+) channel is selectively modulated by impulse activity in a crayfish phasic motor neuron and that this modulation is likely involved in long-term depression of neuromuscular transmission.
the voltage-dependent calcium current recorded from the crayfish motoneurons F3 is composed of at least two subpopulations: one belongs to P-type calcium channels, the other does not.
a P-type Ca2 channel contributes to the macroscopic current in the cell body membrane of a crayfish motoneneuron and that this P-type Ca(2+) current is selectively reduced by impulse activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Ca2+ in the long-term regulation of transmitter release.
the mechanisms by which the motoneuronal cell body controls the activity-dependent modulation of transmitter release at the neuromotor synapses.
the role of impulse activity in the modulation of transmitter release at the crayfish neuromuscular junction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ca2+-dependent long-term reduction of transmitter release is due to a selective reduction in a P-type Ca2+-current.
the P-type Ca(2+ )current is reduced in the F3 motoneuron after a period of intense activity.
the long-term reduction of transmitter release at the crayfish motoneurone synapse is mediated by a reduction of the P-type calcium channel current.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the P-type Ca(2+) channel is the main channel responsible for the Ca(2+) entry into the cell body of motoneuron F-3, and the P-type channel is also the channel that is reduced after the increased impulse activity.
P-type Ca2 channels are modulated by activity and are important for transmitter release.
the P-type Ca(2+) channels are the ones that are reduced by increased activity and that this reduction is the mechanism for the long term reduction in neurotransmitter release.

the P-type Ca ^{2+} current in the crayfish phasic abdominal motoneuron (F3) undergoes a long-lasting reduction as a result from an increase in the frequency of impulse activity, and that this activity-dependent reduction in P-type Ca ^{+} current is likely involved with the long-term depression in neurotransmitter release observed at the synapses of the motoneurons.
